strengths: Well-motivated problem integration addressing genuine limitations of existing approaches (omics-only, text-only, graph-only methods)
Creative technical approach using pretrained GNN as process reward model instead of requiring explicit intermediate annotations
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including multiple baselines, ablation studies across 23+ cancer types, and pathway enrichment validation
Valuable Target-QA benchmark combining CRISPR data, multi-omics, and biomedical knowledge for community use
Strong reproducibility efforts with detailed hyperparameters, training procedures, and promised code/data release
weaknesses: Small dataset (363 QA pairs, 300 train/63 test) with high variance in results (e.g., PRAD ±27% std dev); many cancer types have only 2-7 test samples limiting generalization claims
Modest empirical improvements: GALAX +2-5% over L3-FT(QA) baselines; improvements often within 1-2 standard deviations; absolute precision only ~0.55

Confounded attribution of improvements: massive gain from LLM fine-tuning (L3+Omics: 0.0071 → L3-FT(QA)+Omics: 0.5250) dominates results; unclear if RL/graph component's 2-5% gain justifies complexity

Reward model justification unclear: GPRM trained on binary disease classification, not target discovery; no validation that learned rewards correlate with target accuracy or outperform random graph construction

Critical experimental validation gap: enrichment analyses are post-hoc only; pathway enrichment ≠ functional correctness; no CRISPR validation in independent cell lines; some enrichment results barely significant

Graph construction underspecified: action sampling (πSRC, πTGT) vague; no sensitivity analysis on L, η, K, H; hyperparameter choices appear ad-hoc; greedy acceptance strategy lacks exploration justification

Incomplete baseline analysis: G-Retriever (designed for this task) significantly underperforms with no adequate explanation; weak baselines (M2T precision 0.001); missing comparisons to biomedical foundation models
Limited technical novelty: straightforward integration of existing techniques (LLM + GNN + RL) without novel architectural components or theoretical contributions

strengths: Addresses an important problem in precision medicine requiring integration of multi-modal biomedical data
Proposes a novel combination of LLMs, GNNs, and RL with a GPRM for explainable biomedical reasoning
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple cancer types with detailed ablations and extensive appendices
Includes enrichment analysis validating that predicted genes associate with known biological pathways
Claims to release code and dataset for reproducibility
weaknesses: Critically small dataset: Target-QA has only 363 samples (300 train, 63 test), insufficient for training complex multi-component systems; ground-truth target definitions are vague
Marginal performance improvements (2-5% over G-Retriever baseline) without statistical significance testing; 63 test samples is too small for reliable conclusions
Fundamental question unaddressed: unclear how CRISPR dependency in cell lines translates to effective therapeutic targets; no patient-derived or orthogonal validation
Biological validity concerns: enrichment analysis is post-hoc on training data only; does not demonstrate predicted genes are better targets than others in enriched pathways
Fragile framework: static knowledge graphs hurt performance (Table 1), suggesting poor integration; unstable RL training requiring adaptive hyperparameter tuning (Appendix D.2)
Limited novelty: primarily engineering contribution combining standard components (LLM fine-tuning, GAT, policy gradient RL); GPRM is essentially using a classifier as a reward function

Weak experimental design: incomplete baselines (no comparison to simpler interpretable methods, network propagation, or domain-specific multi-omics approaches); unfair comparisons; no cross-validation

Presentation and clarity: extremely dense paper with critical details scattered across 31-page appendix; problem formulation, methodology, and key concepts (explainability, biological plausibility) are vague or undefined
Questionable foundation model pretraining: GNN edge prediction achieves only 64.4% AUC on 269 training samples; LLM biomedical pretraining uses only 336 samples
Generalization concerns: tested exclusively on DepMap cell lines with circular data dependencies; no evaluation on held-out cancer types or independent datasets

strengths: Novel framework: Clever use of GNNs as process reward models for step-wise supervision without explicit intermediate annotations is an innovative contribution to biomedical AI reasoning
Well-motivated problem formulation: Clear articulation of complementary limitations in existing approaches (siloed multi-omics, text-only LLMs, graph-only models) with natural integration strategy
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Extensive testing across 24+ cancer cohorts with thorough ablation studies showing QA finetuning as dominant factor and consistent 2-5% improvements

Biological grounding and interpretability: Generated subgraphs validated through enrichment analysis against known pathways (EGFR in NSCLC, Wnt signaling in ALL), providing mechanistic insight beyond target rankings
Strong reproducibility: Code and Target-QA benchmark publicly available; extensive hyperparameter details, training curves, and complexity analysis documented
weaknesses: Limited evaluation scope: Only 63 test samples from same CRISPR dataset used to motivate the work; no independent external validation of predicted targets in novel experiments
Small dataset with fragile per-cancer analysis: Several cancer types have only 2-7 test samples; no analysis of learning curves or data scaling properties
Modest improvements with unjustified complexity: 2.2% precision improvement over much simpler baseline (L3-FT(QA): 0.525 vs GALAX: 0.547) does not justify complex multi-stage pipeline with RL

Under-analyzed reinforcement learning design: Reward formulation combines three terms with equal weighting; no sensitivity analysis on hyperparameters (λ, λrule), threshold (R_total > 0), or alternative reward structures
Weak external baselines: G-Retriever is only strong external baseline; most comparisons are ablations of GALAX; no comparison to other recent biomedical LLM-graph methods

Potential circularity in validation: Enrichment analysis uses same pathway databases (WikiPathways, KEGG) that overlap with BioMedGraphica knowledge used as model input, limiting independence of validation
Severe feature filtering bottleneck: Top K=10 features per modality (30 total features) is aggressively reductive; no justification or ablation on this design choice
Missing critical ablations: No ablation isolating RL contribution vs. init/final answering stages; no sensitivity analysis for hyperparameters (K, L, η); no analysis of generated subgraph properties

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing genuine limitations of existing approaches in precision medicine target discovery
Creative reward design using frozen GNN as process reward model with multi-faceted defense against reward hacking
Valuable Target-QA benchmark combining multi-omic, biomedical graph, and CRISPR data across diverse cancer types
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with ablations, generalization studies (holdout cancer types, external PedDep dataset), and biological grounding through enrichment analysis
Biological plausibility validated through pathway enrichment (EGFR in LUAD, TCF3-PBX1 in ALL) and human evaluation
Consistent 2-5% improvements across metrics and multiple cancer types with reproducibility (code release promised)
Thoughtful integration of multiple modalities (numerical omics, text, topology) into unified framework
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: RL formulation uses straightforward rollout-based estimation; primary contribution is engineering/application rather than fundamental innovation
Modest performance improvements: 3-4% gains over strongest baseline (L3-FT(QA)+Omics+KG) at significant added complexity; absolute metrics (~0.54 precision/recall) are reasonable but not exceptional
Dataset limitations: Only 363 samples (300 training, 63 test); limited to cancer cell lines not patient samples; zero-shot transfer drops to 0.29 F1 on external data
Biological validation concerns: enrichment analysis is post-hoc and doesn't validate therapeutic efficacy; human evaluation limited to 3 annotators scoring 10 samples (average score 3.76/5)
RL training stability: retry mechanism with 6 runs and adaptive hyperparameter tuning (Table D.2) suggests instability; no ablation on rollout depth or sensitivity to reward weights
Unfair baseline comparisons: ChatGPT-5.1 used to generate ground-truth reasoning paths for RoG/SubgraphRAG/GNN-RAG, introducing noise; M2T baseline near-zero performance
Presentation and clarity issues: 43 tables make paper dense; 'explainability' not formally defined; missing failure case analysis; notation heavy with many subscripts/superscripts
Graph construction under-specified: candidate node selection sparse; 1-hop subgraph limit not ablated; subgraph size/complexity analysis missing
Computational efficiency not addressed: complexity same as retrieval baselines; 6 RL rollouts per inference; no wall-clock time comparisons or scalability analysis
Reproducibility concerns: NER uses proprietary GPT-4o-mini; DepMap data access restricted; BioMedGraphica from concurrent work
Limited statistical rigor: no significance testing despite error bars; improvements sometimes within standard deviation; no sensitivity analysis for hyperparameters

strengths: Addresses important biomedical problem: CRISPR target discovery in precision medicine
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with multiple baselines, ablation studies, and extensive appendix
Multimodal integration of omics features, biomedical knowledge graphs, and textual information
Attempts biological validation through enrichment analysis and expert human evaluation
Promises to release code and datasets for reproducibility
External validation on PedDep dataset and generalization testing with held-out cancer types
weaknesses: Marginal performance improvements (2-5% F1) over simpler baselines do not justify the added complexity of the 4-stage pipeline
Small dataset: Target-QA has only 363 samples (300 train, 63 test), insufficient for claims about deep learning generalization
Overclaiming key concepts: 'Graph Process Reward Model' is simply frozen GNN + rule checks, not a true process-level reasoning model; 'explainability' is just subgraph visualization
Weak generalization: 10% F1 drop on held-out cancer types (0.54→0.49); external PedDep validation shows F1≈0.29 in zero-shot setting
Evaluation metrics problematic: Hit@5/Hit@10 are inflated (0.92/0.88) when ranking among 100 candidates; precision/recall ~0.54 are only moderate
Ablations suggest components are dispensable: removing graph module, rules, or rollout causes only 0.5-1% performance drops, questioning necessity
Mixed biological validation: human expert evaluation (Table 15) shows mean 3.76/5 with several ratings at 2-3; only 10 samples evaluated
Technical concerns: edge masking uses p=0.0001 (extremely sparse supervision), random oversampling for class imbalance is naive, reward formulation (Eq. 10) lacks justification
Hyperparameter choices (K=10, L=5, η=20, λ=1) are unjustified with no sensitivity analysis; 'retry mechanism' appears to be a training stability hack
No independent clinical validation; no comparison with end-to-end trained graph neural networks or recent biomedical LLMs (BioGPT, PubMedBERT)

strengths: Well-motivated problem integrating multi-modal biomedical data (omics, graphs, text) for interpretable target discovery in precision medicine
Thoughtful system design using Graph Process Reward Model as proxy for biological plausibility without explicit step-wise labels
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 27+ cancer types with 13+ baselines, ablations, hold-out cancer evaluation, external validation, and biological enrichment analysis
Strong biological validation showing identified subgraphs match known cancer pathways (EGFR in NSCLC, TCF3-PBX1 in ALL) with human bioinformatician confirmation
New Target-QA benchmark resource (363 QA pairs combining CRISPR screens, multi-omics, knowledge graphs) with commitment to release code and preprocessing pipelines
Consistent empirical improvements over baselines (2-5% gains in precision/recall/F1; Hit@5 0.9249 vs 0.8794)
Multiple defenses against reward hacking through frozen classifier + rule validation + rollout-based rewards with clear ablation study
weaknesses: Small dataset size (363 QA pairs, 290 train/63 test) raises concerns about overfitting and statistical reliability for deep learning; no learning curves to assess data saturation; hold-out cancer type evaluation shows 10% relative F1 drop (0.5399→0.4862)

Evaluation metric limitations: precision/recall on set overlap is crude without ranking-aware metrics (NDCG, MRR); Jaccard depends entirely on exact match; Hit@5/10 extremely lenient (5-10 of 100 targets); low absolute precision (~55%) raises clinical utility questions

Unfair baseline comparisons: RoG/SubgraphRAG/GNN-RAG required synthesizing reasoning paths using ChatGPT-5.1, introducing systematic noise and disadvantaging methods not originally designed for this task
Unjustified hyperparameter choices: λ=λ_rule=1.0 without ablation or justification; rollout depth L=5, K=10 features, mask rate p=0.0001 lack principled selection or sensitivity analysis

Ground truth validity concerns: CRISPR screen targets are empirically observed, not validated targets; different conditions produce different hits; no validation that matching DepMap targets improves actual therapeutic outcomes
Knowledge graph completeness not addressed: reliance on BioMedGraphica without analyzing coverage, accuracy, or currency; no ablation on KG quality; generalizability to sparse KGs unknown

Method complexity with many components and hyperparameters may limit adoption; prompt engineering dependency with no robustness analysis to variations; 'explainability' primarily amounts to showing constructed subgraph rather than true mechanistic interpretation
